recipes.description: A pre-war hand-crank gramophone. The lacquer is cracked but the mechanism still turns.
recipes.restoration_text: The gramophone crackles to life. A scratchy recording of a string quartet fills the bunker. For three minutes and forty seconds, everyone stops what they're doing and just listens.

recipes.description: A portable film projector, bulb intact but mechanism seized from decades of disuse.
recipes.restoration_text: The projector whirs to life, casting flickering images on the bunker wall. It's an old home movie — a birthday party, a child blowing out candles. No one knows these people. Everyone watches anyway.

recipes.description: A vacuum-tube ham radio transceiver, pre-digital, built to last through anything.
recipes.restoration_text: The radio hums with static, then — a voice. Faint, distant, but unmistakably human. 'Hello? Is anyone out there?' The bunker holds its breath.

recipes.description: A small silver music box, tarnished but intact. The winding key is still attached.
recipes.restoration_text: The music box plays a melody no one recognizes but everyone feels. An old lullaby, maybe. A child hums along, and for just a moment, the bunker feels like a home.

recipes.description: A heavy cast-iron typewriter. The ribbon is dry but the keys still strike true.
recipes.restoration_text: The typewriter's clack fills the quiet hours. Survivors take turns typing letters — to loved ones, to the future, to no one in particular. The paper stacks up like a testament.

recipes.description: A medium-format camera, lenses fogged but body solid. The shutter still clicks.
recipes.restoration_text: The camera captures the bunker in black and white — tired faces, patched walls, small kindnesses. Someone suggests a group portrait. For the first time since the exchange, everyone smiles at once.

recipes.description: A wooden mantel clock with a brass face, stopped at some hour nobody remembers. The case is sound; the movement is gummed with old oil and dust.
recipes.restoration_text: The repaired movement catches after two false starts, then settles into a dry, even ticking. Nobody says much about it. By evening, someone has moved the duty roster so the shift marks line up with the clock.

recipes.description: A cast-iron treadle sewing machine, decals worn to ghosts, belt rotted away. The needle bar still moves freely by hand.
recipes.restoration_text: The wheel turns stiffly at first, then the needle begins finding the same hole twice. A torn sleeve appears on the table before the test strip is finished. Someone has kept it folded for months.

recipes.description: A long brass refractor on a wooden tripod, objective clouded and one eyepiece crushed. The focuser rack is intact and the optics can be re-seated.
recipes.restoration_text: The image swims until the final lens ring is tightened. That night, the shelter takes turns looking through it at a sky they usually check only for weather. For a while, nobody asks whether anything up there is useful.

recipes.description: A small hand-lever press, rollers dried solid and platen off its slides. The frame is heavy cast iron and true; it only wants cleaning, re-seating, and fresh composition.
recipes.restoration_text: The first sheet comes out uneven, one corner darker than the rest. It is only a maintenance notice, but three people read it before it is pinned up. The next sheet carries a name someone wants remembered.

recipes.description: A well-made violin found in a buckled hard case: one string gone, bridge fallen, a clean crack along the flank. The scroll and fingerboard are undamaged.
recipes.restoration_text: The first note catches and breaks. The second holds long enough for the room to go quiet. No one asks for a song; they wait to hear whether there will be a third.

recipes.description: A monocular laboratory microscope with three objectives, focus wheel slipping and stage clips bent. The optics are uncracked and the stand is solid.
recipes.restoration_text: The focus wheel finally stops slipping. Someone places a scrap of onion skin under the glass because it is the first thing close at hand. By supper, half the shelter has looked at something they had spent years eating without ever seeing.

recipes.description: A surveyor's brass compass in a fitted case, needle bearing worn and crystal star-cracked. The card still reads true when the needle is freed.
recipes.restoration_text: The needle trembles, circles once, and settles. A survivor checks it against the shelter map, then checks it again. The instrument tells them nothing new, but the certainty seems to matter.

recipes.description: A pre-war boxed cloth kite, two cells, spars snapped at the joints but recoverable. The tail ribbons are still sewn to the frame.
recipes.restoration_text: The repaired frame is lighter than it looks. When the wind catches it, everyone expects the old cloth to tear; it does not. For several minutes the shelter watches something climb that was never meant to carry supplies, signals, or weapons.

recipes.description: A wall-mounted hand coffee grinder, hopper dented, burrs rusted together. The crank shaft turns after persuasion and the drawer still slides.
recipes.restoration_text: The crank complains through the first turn and smooths out by the fifth. There is barely enough coffee left to justify using it, but someone measures a handful anyway. The smell reaches the corridor before the cups do.

recipes.description: A field-unit hand-crank charger for standard cells. The gearing is stiff but the generator still produces a measurable current when the handle is turned.
A pre-war sintered-bronceramic water filter cartridge. The housing is intact; the medium is fouled but can be reconditioned with charcoal.
A set of three aligned front-silvered mirrors in a folding frame, calibrated for line-of-sight daylight signalling over kilometres of open ground.
A bismuth-telluride junction that produces a trickle of current from a heat differential. Cracked solder joints, but the elements read continuous.
A workshop tool: a hand-cranked drill whose spindle also drives a small alternator. Worn brushes, but the windings still test good.
A kerosene-pressure lantern, tank sound, pump leather perished. Burns bright once re-sealed and the thorium mantle is tied on.
A clockwork interval switch for automating ventilation or grow-lights on a fixed cycle. The escapement is dry but intact.
A three-cup wind-speed gauge with a mechanical counter. Useful for predicting dust storms and scheduling exterior work.
A quartz-fibre dosimeter the size of a pen, with a separate charger-reader. Holds calibration; the fibre drifts but re-zeros cleanly.
A refrigerated coil assembly that condenses potable water from humid air. Compressor seal perished; the coil matrix is sound.
A three-stage transistor amplifier for weak radio signals, point-to-point wired on a tag-strip. Two transistors cracked, the rest test good.
A bench unit that pulses a desulfation cycle into lead-acid cells to recover lost capacity. Meter face cracked, internals intact.
A peristaltic dosing pump that meters nutrient solution into grow beds on a timer. Tubing perished, the pump head and motor are salvageable.
A handheld ultraviolet sterilizer for tool and water disinfection. The tube is intact; the ballast resistor is open-circuit.
A geared hand-crank centrifuge for separating sediment from water samples before filtration. Bearings rough, rotor balanced.
A moving-coil geophone for detecting footsteps or vehicle vibration through rock. The coil is open; the suspension is intact.
A military fire-control computer for a perimeter turret: IFF transponder, lead-computing sight, interlock relay. Three boards cracked, the CPU core is intact.
A military manpack transceiver with a burst-encryption module and a frequency-hopping synthesizer. The crypto board is wiped; the RF chain is recoverable.
A short-range air-search radar display and receiver, pack-mounted. The magnetron is spent; the waveguide and scope are serviceable.
A military exoskeleton limb servo: harmonic drive, torque sensor, fail-safe brake. The gearbox is dry; the motor windings test good.
A shaped charge assembly engineered for breaching hardened vault doors, with a redundant dual-initiator. The explosive is inert; the engineering is the prize.
An Identification-Friend-or-Foe transponder with a coded-reply module. The encryption PROM is erased; the RF deck and timing logic are intact.
A military chemical-biological-radiological-nuclear overpressure filter bank for a bunker air system. The HEPA is spent; the activated carbon and housing are sound.
A military field-hospital robotic arm for remote suturing and debridement under telemetry. Two joints seized; the stepper drivers and force sensors are intact.
